title: span-clustering-and-annotations-brainstorm
content:
Context and goal:

This doc collects ideas for improving the request tracing UI in the Console with a focus on: making long traces scannable, enabling lightweight developer notes/annotations on spans, and adding clustering/grouping so repeated or noisy spans don't distract from the signal. Primarily targeted at SREs and backend engineers who need to find root cause quickly in production traces.

User stories:
- As an SRE I want fast visual grouping of repeated span types (e.g., cache-check x100) so I can focus on the unusual spans.
- As an engineer I want to leave a short note on a span ("Db index missing") so teammates see context when they inspect that span later.
- As a support engineer I want to search for traces by custom attribute (region:eu, host:gpu-2) and jump to the first span matching that attribute.

High-level interactions / proposals:
1) Adaptive span clustering (default folded)
   - Detect repeated siblings by signature: same operation name, same service, similar duration distribution.
   - UI: show one representative row with a fold chevron and a small count badge (e.g., "x84").
   - Expand reveals the individual spans inline. The expanded state persists per-trace view until closed.
   - Keyboard: when folded, pressing Enter expands; when expanded, Enter collapses.

2) Span annotations and lightweight comments
   - Inline note: small icon on the right of span row. Click to add a 1-2 sentence note. Notes are versioned (timestamp + author).
   - Notes visible to anyone who opens the trace; optional private/team-level visibility toggle in settings.
   - Acceptance criteria: add note -> appears in span details and hovercards; note stored as metadata on trace/span.

3) Signal-first coloring and percentile badges
   - Color spans by deviation from expected duration for that operation (green = within p50, orange = p90, red = >p99). This surfaces anomalous spans in long traces.
   - Show a tiny percentile badge next to duration (e.g., "p97").

4) Time scrubber, mini-map, and sticky markers
   - Mini-map at bottom provides overview and allows rubberband zoom across timeline.
   - Add sticky markers for annotated spans so you can jump between notes. Markers are numbered and match note order.

5) Detail panel and hovercard parity
   - Hovercard shows: op name, service, duration, start offset, tags/attributes, top 3 related logs (if any), link to session replay/logs.
   - Clicking a span opens right-side detail panel (persisting when exploring other spans). Panel contains notes, full attributes, derived attribution (network/db/compute).

6) Search and filter DSL (small-powerful search)
   - Single-line search supports attribute filters and regex: e.g., "service:ingest status_code:>=500 /timeout/".
   - Filter chips appear under search bar; clicking toggles. Provide a breadcrumb of active filters.

7) Copyable deep-linking and permalinks
   - Every span has a deep-link that captures trace id + span id + optional viewport (zoom level and time window).
   - Use-case: include in an incident slack message so teammates open the exact span and zoom.

8) Comparison overlay (lightweight)
   - Allow selecting 2 traces and overlay their waterfalls to compare operation timing side-by-side or superimposed (opacity). Useful for regressions after a deploy.

Rendering & performance constraints:
- Many traces will be large (>1000 spans). The waterfall must be virtualized; rows should render only when visible.
- Clustering should operate client-side on the streamed trace when the full trace is available; show progressive clustering as spans arrive.
- Keep hovercards fetch-light: prefer attributes already present in the trace payload, only request logs on demand.

Accessibility and keyboard navigation:
- Tab focus order: search -> filters -> waterfall -> detail panel.
- Arrow keys move between spans; shift+arrow to multi-select.
- Provide aria-labels for fold/unfold and annotation icons.

Edge cases and unresolved decisions:
- Should annotations be editable after creation? (pro: correct mistakes; con: change history complexity)
- Team/private annotation visibility scope: per-org, per-team, per-user? Default to org-level with opt-out.
- How to persist expanded/collapsed state across sessions? Local storage vs server-side user prefs.

Backlog candidates (rough priority)
- P0: Basic foldable clustering + count badges + hovercard improvements. (AC: fold/unfold, counts display, no regressions on small traces)
- P1: Annotations (create/view) + deep-links to annotated spans. (AC: store notes, show in UI, link with timestamp/author)
- P1: Percentile coloring + percentile badges. (AC: compute percentiles via precomputed profiles or on-the-fly sample)
- P2: Mini-map + rubberband zoom + sticky markers for notes.
- P2: Lightweight trace overlay compare.
- P3: Private/team annotations + edit history + annotations API.

Wireframe sketches (textual)
- Top bar: [search field] [filter chips area] [time-range selector] [compare traces button]
- Left column: trace list + quick stats (trace duration, errors)
- Middle: waterfall canvas with rows (fold chevron | op name | service pill | duration badge | percentile badge | annotations icon)
- Bottom mini-map: small timeline with highlighted visible window and numbered markers for notes
- Right panel: span details (notes, attributes, related logs, open in logs button, open session replay)

Quick interaction flows:
- "Find first database timeout": search "op:db /timeout/" -> first matching span auto-focused -> detail panel opens showing related logs -> user adds an annotation -> copy deep-link -> paste into incident thread.
- "Investigate noisy cache hits": open trace -> clusters folded -> expand representative cluster -> reveal heavy tail span -> color shows p99 -> add note and create alert from span.

Telemetry and metrics to track post-launch:
- % of traces with clusters auto-collapsed vs expanded.
- Annotation creation rate (per org/team).
- Time-to-first-action (open span -> take action like copy link / create alert).
- Average render time for traces with >500 spans.

Related tickets / next steps:
- JIRA-TRC-982: backend: attach annotation metadata to span model (auth + visibility).
- FE spike: virtualized waterfall rendering + cluster algorithm (contrib: Diego).
- UX: create hi-fidelity mockups for fold/unfold animation and annotation modal.

Open questions for the next grooming session:
- Default clustering threshold (exact signature vs fuzzy similarity).
- User preference for auto-expand when search matches a folded cluster.
- How to expose sampling/partial-trace indicators so users don't misinterpret missing spans.

Notes to self:
- Prototype SVG-based waterfall (Canvas may be faster for 2k+ spans). Test both with sample production traces.
- Check privacy implications of free-text annotations for regulated customers (PII detection?).

END
